briefdescription.para: Gets the time elapsed between start() and stop().

detaileddescription.para: The interval is truncated to whole microseconds. Without both readings (see has_elapsed()), the elapsed time is zero.

Parameters
None.
The elapsed time, in microseconds.
Converts the differences of the seconds and of the nanoseconds members to a single nanoseconds duration, so that a negative nanoseconds difference borrows from the seconds without explicit normalisation, and truncates the result to whole microseconds. If has_elapsed() is false, the result is zero.

briefdescription.para: Records the start time, from the system clock.

detaileddescription.para: Each call restarts the measurement: the stop reading is cleared, so has_elapsed() is false until the next stop().

Clears both readings, then reads the system clock into start_time_. The readings are cleared first because read_clock() leaves its argument unchanged on the platforms without a clock, where a previous reading would otherwise survive.

Clears the stop reading, then reads the system clock into stop_time_, for the same reason as in start(). The start reading is not changed.

Reads the system clock into start_time_ only if is_recorded() reports no start reading; since the reading is zero in that case, it need not be cleared first, as in start().

briefdescription.para: Checks whether a clock reading was recorded.

detaileddescription.para: A zero timespec means that the clock was not read, or that the platform has no clock.

ts
The clock reading to check.
true
At least one of the members is not zero.
false
Both members are zero.
Returns true if at least one of the tv_sec or tv_nsec members of ts is non-zero, indicating that a clock reading was captured.

briefdescription.para: Measures the elapsed time of an operation.

detaileddescription.para: start() reads the system clock just before the measured operation and stop() just after it; when both readings are available, elapsed() returns the interval between them.

Each call reads the clock again: start() restarts the measurement, discarding both previous readings, and stop() replaces the previous stop reading, if any. A zero reading means that the clock was not read, either because the stopwatch was not started (or stopped), or because the platform has no clock; in both cases has_elapsed() returns false, so that the reporters can skip the timing output.

Typical usage in the framework:
Call start() just before the test suite or session body executes.
Call stop() immediately after it completes.
The reporters display elapsed(), when has_elapsed().
The class is non-copyable and non-movable to prevent accidental sharing of live timing state.
The non-public members are protected, not private, only so that the unit tests can derive from the class and set known readings; the class is not meant to be extended otherwise.

The public members of the v5.0.1 detail::timestamps class (timestamp_begin(), timestamp_end(), has_begin(), has_end(), has_timestamps(), and compute_elapsed_time()) are kept, deprecated, for the applications that used the deprecated timings() of the runner and of the suites, which return a reference to this class.
